title: eval-trigger-hash-ledger-for-promptset-immutability
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an append-only hash ledger service that anchors prompt set and golden dataset snapshots to cryptographic hashes tied to config and model-change events. The ledger will provide tamper-evident mappings from: promptset-id + version + config-hash -> eval-run-id(s). This enables deterministic regression detection and forensic traceability when a config or model roll produces a quality delta. Goals: (1) immutable snapshot references for every eval-trigger, (2) signed ledger entries using customer KMS for enterprise Private installs, and (3) a small query API used by console and CI to map failing regressions to the exact promptset snapshot and config that caused them.
acceptance_criteria: Ledger service persists entries with monotonic sequence and cryptographic hash of prompt bundle + config + model-commit
API endpoint /ledger/lookup can return promptset snapshot URI and list of eval-run-ids for a given config-hash within 200ms 99th percentile
Entries optionally carry KMS-based signatures for private deployments; signing flow documented in confluence
Console can call ledger API and show 'source snapshot' link from regression detail pane
Migration: replay last 90 days of promptset evals into ledger without blocking current eval pipeline
tasks: design API schema and sequence model (ENG design doc)
implement lightweight append-only store (Postgres table + hash index)
KMS signing integration for Private (support AWS KMS + Azure Key Vault)
CI hook to write ledger entry on eval-trigger (job-level write)
console integration: add lookup and link to snapshot viewer
write migration job to backfill recent evals into ledger
load-test ledger for 1000 writes/s burst and 10k reads/s
blockers: KMS access pattern for Private: need clarity on HSM signing performance from Security
storage schema review: trade-offs between append-only table vs LSM store (need infra/DB lead sign-off)
comments: 2025-02-11 | Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes attached. Decided on canonical payload: promptset_tarball_sha256, config_json_sha256, model_commit_sha, eval_run_id, timestamp, prev_entry_hash
2025-02-18 | Carlos Mendes: Proof-of-concept done. Using Postgres with pgcrypto for hashing. Observed 2ms median insert latency on dev cluster. POC branch: github.com/redwood-inference/ledger/poc

2025-02-22 | Security (Marta Li): We require KMS-signed envelope for Private tenants. Need key rotation plan and offline verification path. Security to provide KMS-API SLA for signing latency by 2025-03-03

2025-02-28 | Product (Ravi Shah): Console UX is fine with a single 'Snapshot linked' badge; prefer to show both promptset version and config diff summary. PM asked for ability to filter regressions by config-hash in Console

2025-03-04 | Carlos Mendes: Began migration job to backfill last 90 days. Running in dry-run; estimate full run will take ~3 hours against prod-analytics. Observed one mismatch where prompt bundle tarball missing (edge case: deleted tmp artifact). Added retry+rebuild path to tasks.
notes: Trade-offs considered: full Merkle tree across all promptsets vs per-snapshot hash chaining. Chosen per-snapshot chain to keep query simple for Console and avoid expensive tree rebalances.
We will expose ledger lookups to internal CI and Console only; external customer API exposure is out-of-scope for initial ship.
Consider future: anchor ledger roots to a public transparency log (optional) for highest-assurance customers. Keep schema flexible to add external anchors later.
